about.title: Guadalupe Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Guadalupe's economy runs on hands-on work — agriculture, packing, trucking, and the small businesses that line Guadalupe Street and 11th Street. That kind of labor comes with real risk, whether it's a forklift accident, a fall from equipment, or a collision while making a delivery near W Main Street. Under California law, workers' compensation is typically the first and exclusive path against your employer, no matter who was at fault. But if a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate third-party claim worth pursuing. Sorting out which path applies — or whether both do — takes a careful look at what happened and who was involved. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect injured workers in Guadalupe with an independent attorney who can walk through the details and explain your options, without any upfront cost or obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Workplace Injury

items.title: Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can open a separate injury claim worth exploring.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, so timing your next steps correctly can protect your options going forward.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: Your employer cannot legally punish or fire you for reporting an injury or filing a claim, and an attorney can help you understand what protections apply to your situation.

items.question: I was hurt on a delivery run near W Main Street — is that a workers' comp case or something else?
items.answer: It could be both. If another driver caused the crash while you were working, you may have a workers' comp claim against your employer and a separate third-party claim against the at-fault driver. An independent attorney can look at the details of the collision and sort out which claims apply.

items.question: Can I still get help if my employer says my injury doesn't qualify for workers' comp?
items.answer: Yes — disputes over whether an injury qualifies happen often, and you're not required to accept your employer's first answer. An attorney can review the situation and explain what options may still be available to you.

items.question: What if the equipment I was using at work turned out to be defective?
items.answer: If a piece of equipment or machinery failed and caused your injury, that could support a third-party claim against the manufacturer separate from any workers' comp benefits. These claims carry a 2-year deadline in California, so it's worth having someone look into it sooner rather than later.
